raw_response:
Eh, you want to know how I'll manage the land this year? Let me think it through. I've been doing this 15 years, so I mostly know what works on my plots, but every year is a little different.

My 10.1 mu — I split it like this: about 6 mu is wheat-maize rotation (the good flat pieces near the road), and the other 4 mu is cotton. I've kept this split for years now. The cotton gives me cash from selling to the gin, and the wheat-maize feeds the family and gives some grain to sell. My old man helps with the heavy work, and when it's cotton picking time my daughter-in-law comes back from town to help. Labor is my biggest worry now that I'm 70 — I can't bend over in the cotton field like I used to.

**Wheat (already planted last October, ~6 mu)**

The wheat went in around October 10th last year, Jimai 22 variety — same seed I've used for years, the extension station recommended it a while back and it does well enough on my soil. I already put down about 8 kg of urea per mu plus a bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before sowing, that's my base. Now it's jointing, so I need to topdress. I'll put another 10 kg urea per mu this week along with the jointing irrigation. If the heads look thin at heading I might give another small irrigation, but water from the well isn't cheap — electricity for pumping adds up. Probably 2-3 irrigations total depending on rain. I'll spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, my neighbor Old Wang always sprays so I go with him and we share the sprayer. Hoping for around 450 kg/mu, which is what I usually get.

**Maize (plant mid-June right after wheat harvest, ~6 mu)**

Very tight window — I hire the combine for wheat harvest so the straw gets chopped, then I'll hire the no-till seeder to plant maize the same day or next day. No time to really till. I use Zhengdan 958 seed, the neighbors all use it, costs about 50 yuan/mu for seed. I put compound fertilizer down at planting with the seeder, then topdress urea once at big trumpet stage — about 12 kg N/mu total, maybe a bit more if I have money. Maize usually doesn't need much irrigation here in summer because of the rains, but if July is dry I'll give one watering. One herbicide spray after planting for weeds. Expecting 480 kg/mu, maybe 500 in a good year.

**Cotton (planting now, end of April, 4 mu)**

This is the hard one. I'm planting this week — the ground has warmed up. I use a local variety seed I bought from the township store, about 40 yuan/mu. I put compound fertilizer and some urea in the furrow before planting. Cotton needs less N than wheat, I do about 12 kg N/mu total, splitting it — some at planting, some at flowering. Plastic mulch film over the rows, that's the standard here, keeps the soil warm and saves water. I'll irrigate maybe twice — once after emergence if dry, once at flowering. The hard part is pest control: I have to spray 4-5 times through the season for bollworm and aphids, that's the biggest cost. Picking starts in September and goes through October — 3 or 4 pickings by hand. My daughter-in-law and I do it, sometimes I hire a neighbor woman for a few days at 80 yuan/day. Hoping for 250 kg lint/mu, which sells for decent money if prices hold.

Money-wise, I watch every yuan. My total input cost is around 4,000 yuan for the whole 10.1 mu. I don't have spare cash to experiment with new things — if something worked last year I do it again. Only change I'm thinking about this year: the extension man came around and said I should try less urea on maize because it just washes away, but I'm not sure, I'll probably do the same as last year to be safe.
